parsed.why: Shield law plus 1993 gender-identity anti-discrimination covering public accommodations, hate-crime coverage and trans-panic repeal; but documented state custody placement by birth sex (2012) and the federal border/custody regime cap it.

Most Protective tier: shield law, 2011 anti-discrimination, strengthened hate-crime coverage, and custody per recognised gender including strip searches and housing — a working remedy on a tier-1 axis; federal document regime still applies.

Second-worst tier: schools/colleges facility use fixed by birth certificate (unenforced, no penalty), care/sports ban in litigation, no gender-identity discrimination or conversion-therapy law; narrow visitor reach but hostile institutions.

Among worst states: birth-certificate markers closed, law restricts trans bathroom use in many state-run facilities, no public-accommodations protection, hate-crime law excludes gender identity, care and sports bans in force.

Most Protective tier with direct visitor reach: public-accommodations law covers hotels and restaurants, gender-neutral restrooms required, care shield extends to interstate travellers, hate-crime coverage, trans-panic repeal.
